42.h: 38 - Kulthūm ibn al-Hidm ibn Imriʾ al-Qays ibn al-Ḥārith al-Anṣārī *
42.t:
Ibn Zayd ibn ʿUbayd ibn Zayd ibn Mālik ibn ʿAwf ibn ʿAmr ibn ʿAwf ibn Mālik ibn al-Aws al-Anṣārī, al-ʿAwfī, elder of the Anṣār, and the one with whom the Prophet ﷺ stayed when he first came to Medina, at Qubāʾ, when he had become old.
The author of al-Ṭabaqāt said: أنبأنا محمد بن عمر، حدثنا مجمع بن يعقوب، عن سعيد بن عبد الرحمن بن رقيش، عن عبد الرحمن بن يزيد بن جارية، عن عمه مجمع. (ح) .
وأنبأنا محمد بن عمر، حدثنا ابن أبي سبرة، عن عثمان بن وثاب، عن أبي غطفان، عن ابن عباس، قالا:
Kulthūm ibn al-Hidm was a noble man and advanced in years; he accepted Islam before the Prophet ﷺ came to Medina, and when he emigrated, he stayed with him.
He used to hold conversation in the house of Saʿd ibn Khaythamah, which was called: the house of the bachelors (2) . ⟦1:242⟧
For that reason al-Wāqidī said:
It was said: The Prophet ﷺ stayed with Saʿd ibn Khaythamah, and a group of the Emigrants stayed with Kulthūm ibn al-Hidm.
Not long afterwards he died (may Allah be pleased with him), and that was before Badr, and he was a righteous man (1) .

43.h: 39 - Abū Dujānah al-Anṣārī Simāk ibn Kharashah ibn Lawdhān *
43.t:
Ibn ʿAbd Wadd ibn Zayd al-Sāʿidī.
On the day of Uḥud he wore a red headband.
It is said: The Prophet ﷺ established brotherhood between him and ʿUtbah ibn Ghazwān.
al-Wāqidī said: Abū Dujānah stood firm on the day of Uḥud with the Prophet ﷺ, and pledged to him to the death.
He was one of those who took part in killing Musaylimah the Liar, and was then martyred on that day (2) .
Muḥammad ibn Saʿd said: Abū Dujānah has descendants in Medina and in Baghdad to this day.
Zayd ibn Aslam said: He visited Abū Dujānah while he was ill, and his face was shining.
It was said to him: Why is your face shining?
He said: There is no deed I rely on more than two: I would not speak of what did not concern me, and the other was that my heart was sound toward the Muslims (3) . ⟦1:243⟧
And from Anas ibn Mālik, who said:
On the day of al-Yamāmah Abū Dujānah threw himself into the garden, and his leg was broken, and he fought with his leg broken until he was killed (may Allah be pleased with him (1)) .
It is also said: He is Simāk ibn Aws ibn Kharashah.
Ṣāliḥ ibn Mūsā: عن سهيل بن أبي صالح، عن أبيه، عن أبي هريرة، قال:
When the war laid down its burdens, the Companions (الصحابي) of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ boasted of their days, while Ṭalḥah was silent and did not speak, and Simāk ibn Kharashah Abū Dujānah was silent and did not speak (2) .
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said when he saw their silence: (I saw myself on the day of Uḥud, with no created being near me on the earth except Jibrīl on my right and Ṭalḥah on my left (3)) .
The sword of Abū Dujānah was not to be blamed.
That was because the Prophet ﷺ held out that sword until he said: (Who will take this sword with its right?) .
The people held back from it.
Abū Dujānah said: And what is its right, O Messenger of Allah?
He said: (That you fight with it in the way of Allah until Allah grants you victory, or you are killed) .
So he took it on that condition.
Then, before the rout on the day of Uḥud, he went out with his sword drawn, strutting proudly, wearing nothing but a shirt and a red turban with which he had bound his head, and he was reciting verses of rajaz, saying: ⟦1:244⟧
I am a man whom my beloved made a covenant with ... when we were at the foot of the mountain by the date palms
That I would never stay in the fetters for all time ... I strike with the sword of Allah and the Messenger
He said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: (That is a gait (1) that Allah and His Messenger hate, except in a place like (2) this (3)) .
As for the amulet of Abū Dujānah, it is something that is not authentic (الصحيح); I do not know who fabricated it (4) . ⟦1:245⟧

44.h: 40 - Khubayb ibn ʿAdī ibn ʿĀmir ibn Majdaʿah al-Anṣārī *
44.t:
Ibn Jaḥjabā al-Anṣārī, the martyr.
Ibn Saʿd mentioned him, saying: He was present at Uḥud, and he was among those whom the Prophet ﷺ sent with the Banū Liḥyān; when they reached al-Rajīʿ they betrayed them, called for help against them, killed some of them, and captured Khubayb and Zayd ibn al-Dathinah, and sold the two of them in Mecca, and they killed them in retaliation for those of their people whom the Prophet ﷺ had killed, and crucified them at al-Tanʿīm (1) .
Maslamah ibn Jundab said, from al-Ḥārith ibn al-Barṣāʾ, who said:
Khubayb was brought and sold in Mecca, and they took him out to the unconsecrated land to kill him, and he said: Let me pray two rakʿahs. Then ⟦1:246⟧ he said: Were it not that you would think it was fear, I would have prayed more. O Allah, count them one by one.
Al-Ḥārith said: And I was present, and by Allah, I did not think that any of us would remain.
Ibn Isḥāq, from ʿĀṣim ibn ʿUmar, said:
When ʿAḍal and al-Qārah betrayed Khubayb and his companions at al-Rajīʿ, they brought him and Yazīd ibn al-Dathinah. As for Khubayb, ⟦1:247⟧ Ḥujayr ibn Abī Ihāb bought him for ʿUqbah ibn al-Ḥārith ibn ʿĀmir, who was Ḥujayr’s brother through his mother, so that he could kill him in revenge for his father.
When they took him out to kill him, having set up his wooden stake to crucify him, he reached al-Tanʿīm and said:
If you see fit to let me pray two rakʿahs.
They said: Go ahead.
So he prayed, then said: By Allah, were it not that you would think I was prolonging out of fear of death, I would have prayed more.
So he was the first to establish the prayer at the time of execution.
Then they raised him on his stake, and he said: O Allah, count them one by one, and kill them scattered, and leave none of them, O Allah, we have conveyed the message of Your Messenger, so convey to him this morning what has been done to us.
He said: And Muʿāwiyah said: I was among those who attended him, and I saw Abū Sufyān throwing me to the ground out of fear of Khubayb’s supplication.
And they used to say (1) : When a man is cursed and lies down on his side, the supplication slips away from him.
Ibn Isḥāq said: Yaḥyā ibn ʿAbbād narrated to me, from his father, from ʿUqbah ibn al-Ḥārith, who said:
By Allah, I did not kill him, for I was too young for that; but Abū Maysarah al-ʿAbdarī took my hand and put the spear on my hand, then put his hand on my hand, and took it with it, then killed him (2) .
ʿAbd Allāh ibn Idrīs: ʿAmr ibn ʿUthmān ibn Mawhab, client (المولى) of al-Ḥārith ibn ʿĀmir, narrated to me, saying:
Mawhab said: Khubayb said to me - they had placed him with me -: I ask three things of you ⟦1:248⟧ of you: that you give me sweet water to drink, that you keep from me what was slaughtered for the idols, and that you inform me when they intend to kill me (1) .
Ibn Isḥāq: حدثنا ابن أبي نجيح، عن ماوية مولاة حجير، and Khubayb had been imprisoned in her house, and she used to narrate after she accepted Islam, saying:
By Allah, he was imprisoned when I looked in on him from the gap of the door, and in his hand was a cluster of grapes the size of a man’s head, from which he was eating, and I knew of no grape on the earth; then he asked me for a razor to shave himself (2) .

45.h: 41 - Muʿādh ibn ʿAmr ibn al-Jamūḥ ibn Kaʿb al-Anṣārī *
45.t:
Al-Khazrajī, al-Sulamī, al-Madanī, Badrī (البدري), al-ʿAqabī, the killer of Abū Jahl.
Jarīr ibn Ḥāzim said:
From Ibn Isḥāq: Muʿādh ibn ʿAmr ibn al-Jamūḥ ibn Zayd ibn Ḥarām ibn Kaʿb ibn Ghanm ibn Kaʿb ibn Salimah was present at Badr. ⟦1:249⟧
Narrating from him: ابن عباس, and he lived until the late part of the caliphate (الخلافة) of ʿUmar.
And in the two Ṣaḥīḥs (الصحيحين), by way of Yūsuf ibn al-Mājishūn: أنبأنا صالح بن إبراهيم بن عبد الرحمن بن عوف، عن أبيه، عن جده، قال:
I was standing in the rank on the day of Badr, and I looked, and there I was between two youths of the Anṣār, young in years, and I wished to be between stronger men than they.
One of them nudged me and said: O uncle! Do you know Abū Jahl?
I said: Yes, and what do you want with him?
He said: I was told that he insults the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. By Him in whose hand is my soul, if I see him, my shadow will not leave his shadow until the one of us who is fated to die first dies.
I was amazed at that.
Then the other nudged me and said the same, and it was not long (1) before I looked and saw Abū Jahl moving about among the people, and I said:
Do you not see? That is your man.
He said: They rushed at him with their swords until they killed him, then went back to the Prophet ﷺ and told him.
He said: (Which of you killed him?) .
Each of them said: I killed him.
He said: (Have you wiped your swords?) .
They said: No.
He looked at the two swords and said: (You both killed him) .
And he ruled that his spoils belonged to Muʿādh ibn ʿAmr; the other was Muʿādh ibn ʿAfrāʾ (2) .
And from Muʿādh ibn ʿAmr, who said:
I made Abū Jahl my concern on the day of Badr, and when I was able to, I charged at him and struck him, and cut off his foot at the middle of the shin.
His son ʿIkrimah ibn Abī Jahl struck me on my shoulder and threw off my arm, and it remained hanging by a piece of skin at my side, and the fighting kept me ⟦1:250⟧ from it, so I fought for most of my day, dragging it behind me.
When it pained me, I put my foot on it, then stretched upon it until I threw it off (1) .
This, by Allah, is bravery, not like one who is scratched by an arrow and his heart is cut, and his strength gives way.
Ibn Isḥāq related this story, and said: Then he lived after that until the time of ʿUthmān.
He said: And Muʿawwidh ibn ʿAfrāʾ passed by Abū Jahl, and struck him until he laid him low, and left him with a trace of life in him.
Then Muʿawwidh fought until he was killed, and his brother ʿAwf was killed before him, and they were the two sons of al-Ḥārith ibn Rifāʿah al-Zuraqī.
Then Ibn Masʿūd passed by Abū Jahl, and rebuked him while he had a trace of life, then cut off his head.
أخبرنا أحمد بن سلامة، عن ابن مسعود الجمال، أنبأنا أبو علي، أنا أبو نعيم، حدثنا سليمان بن أحمد، حدثنا أحمد الأبار، حدثنا الهيثم بن خارجة، حدثنا رشدين بن سعد، عن عبد الله بن الوليد التجيبي، عن أبي منصور مولى الأنصار، أنه سمع عمرو بن الجموح يقول:
إنه سمع رسول الله ﷺ يقول: (Allah the Mighty and Majestic said: Truly My friends among My servants, and My beloved among My creation, are those who are remembered by My remembrance, and I am remembered by their remembrance) (2) . ⟦1:251⟧
Rishdīn was alone in narrating it, and he is weak (ضعيف).
This hadith does not belong to the subject of the entry, but to his father.
And they have said that ʿAmr was killed on the day of Uḥud, so how could Abū Manṣūr have heard from him?!

46.h: 42 - Muʿawwidh ibn ʿAmr ibn al-Jamūḥ al-Anṣārī al-Sulamī *
46.t: He was present at Badr with his two brothers Muʿādh and Khallād, but Ibn Isḥāq did not mention him, and Allah knows best.

47.h: 43 - Khallād ibn ʿAmr ibn al-Jamūḥ al-Anṣārī **
47.t:
He was present at Badr, and was martyred on the day of Uḥud.
And their father:

48.h: 44 - ʿAmr ibn al-Jamūḥ ibn Zayd ibn Ḥarām al-Sulamī ***
48.t:
Ibn Kaʿb ibn Ghanm ibn Kaʿb (1) ibn Salimah ibn Saʿd ibn ʿAlī ibn Asad ibn Sārdah ibn Tazīd ibn Jusham ibn al-Khazraj al-Anṣārī, al-Sulamī, al-Ghanmī, father of Muʿādh, Muʿawwidh and Khallād, mentioned above, and of ʿAbd al-Raḥmān and Hind. ⟦1:252⟧
Thābit al-Bunānī narrated, from ʿIkrimah, who said:
Muṣʿab ibn ʿUmayr came to Medina to teach the people, and ʿAmr ibn al-Jamūḥ sent to him: What is this that you have brought us?
They said: If you wish we will come to you and let you hear the Qurʾān.
He said: Yes.
So he recited the opening part of Sūrat Yūsuf, and ʿAmr said: We have a consultation to make among our people - and he was the chief of the Banū Salimah.
They left, and he went in to Manāf (1) and said: O Manāf! By Allah, you know that the people want no one but you, so do you have any denial?
He said: Then he hung the sword on him, and went out, and his family rose and took the sword.
When he returned, he said: Where is the sword, O Manāf? Woe to you! Even the she-goat defends its rear; by Allah, I see no good in Abū Jaʿār tomorrow.
Then he said to them: I am going to my property, so treat Manāf well.
He went, and they took him, broke him, tied him with a dead dog, and threw him into a well.
When he came, he said: How are you?
They said: Well, our master; Allah has purified our houses of filth.
He said: By Allah, I think you have done badly in succeeding me with Manāf.
They said: There he is, look at him in that well.
He looked down, saw him, and sent for his people, and they came, and he said: Are you not upon what I am upon?
They said: Indeed, you are our master.
He said: Then I call you to witness that I have believed in what was sent down to Muḥammad.
He said: Then on the day of Uḥud, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: (Rise to a Paradise whose breadth is the heavens and the earth, prepared for the God-fearing) .
He rose, though he was lame, and said: By Allah, I will surely hobble (2) upon it in Paradise.
So he fought until he was killed.
And from ʿĀṣim ibn ʿUmar: that the acceptance of Islam by ʿAmr ibn al-Jamūḥ was delayed, and he had an idol called Manāf, and the young men of the Banū Salimah had believed, and they would wait, until when the night had passed ⟦1:253⟧ they would enter the house of his idol and throw it, head-down, into the foulest pit.
When ʿAmr woke, that distressed him, and he would take it, wash it and perfume it, then they would return to the same deed, until ʿAmr saw how things stood, and became a Muslim.
He composed verses, among them:
By Allah, if you were a god you would not be ... you and a dog in the middle of a well in a rope
Fie on your abode, a god found wanting ... now we have searched you out from the worst of deceptions (1)
He narrated: محمد بن مسلم، عن عمرو بن دينار (ح) ، وفطر بن خليفة، عن حبيب بن أبي ثابت (ح) ، وابن عيينة، عن ابن المنكدر:
That the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: (O Banū Salimah! Who is your chief?) .
They said: Al-Jadd ibn Qays, though we consider him stingy.
He said: (And what disease is worse than stinginess? Rather (2) your chief is the white, curly-haired one: ʿAmr ibn al-Jamūḥ (3)) .
al-Wāqidī said: He was not present at Badr, as he was lame, and when they went out on the day of Uḥud his sons prevented him, and said: Allah has excused you.
He went to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ complaining of them.
He said: (There is no harm if you do not prevent him; perhaps Allah will grant him martyrdom) (4) . ⟦1:254⟧
His wife Hind, the sister of ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAmr ibn Ḥarām, said: It is as though I see him, having taken his small shield, saying: O Allah, do not turn me back; and he was killed, he and his son Khallād.
Isrāʾīl: عن سعيد بن مسروق، عن أبي الضحى:
That ʿAmr ibn al-Jamūḥ said to his sons: You prevented me from Paradise on the day of Badr; by Allah, if I live, I will surely enter Paradise.
When the day of Uḥud came, ʿUmar said: I had no concern but him, so I sought him, and there he was in the first detachment (1) .
Mālik said: He and ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAmr ibn Ḥarām were shrouded in one shroud.
Mālik, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Abī Ṣaʿṣaʿah, that it had reached him:
That the flood had damaged the grave of ʿAmr ibn al-Jamūḥ and of Ibn Ḥarām, so they were dug up for them to be moved from their place, and they were found unchanged, as though they had died the day before; and one of them had been wounded and had put his hand on his wound and was buried like that, and his hand was removed from his wound, then released, and it returned as it had been; and between the day of Uḥud and the day they were dug up was forty-six years (2) . ⟦1:255⟧

49.h: 45 - ʿUbaydah ibn al-Ḥārith ibn al-Muṭṭalib ibn ʿAbd Manāf ibn Quṣayy al-Qurashī al-Muṭṭalibī *
49.t:
His mother was from Thaqīf.
He was one of the first forerunners, and he was ten years older than the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.
He emigrated together with his brothers al-Ṭufayl and Ḥuṣayn; he was of medium height, handsome, and held a great station with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.
He was the one who dueled the chief of the polytheists on the day of Badr; the two exchanged two blows, and each of them incapacitated the other, and ʿAlī and Ḥamzah charged at ʿUtbah and killed him, and carried ʿUbaydah while he had a trace of life; then he died at al-Ṣafrāʾ (1) , in the last ten days of Ramaḍān, in the year 2 (may Allah be pleased with him).
The Prophet ﷺ had appointed him over sixty riders from the Emigrants and tied a banner for him, and it was the first banner tied in Islam; he met Quraysh, led by Abū Sufyān, at Thaniyyat al-Murrah, and that was the first fighting that took place in Islam.
Ibn Isḥāq said it (2) . ⟦1:256⟧

50.h: 46 - Rabīʿah ibn al-Ḥārith ibn ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib ibn Hāshim al-Hāshimī *
50.t:
Abū Arwā.
His children were: Muḥammad, ʿAbd Allāh, al-Ḥārith, al-ʿAbbās, Umayyah, ʿAbd Shams, ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib, Arwā the Elder, Hind, Arwā and Ādam.
As for Ādam: he was the one placed with a wet nurse among Hudhayl, and the Banū Layth ibn Bakr killed him in a war that took place among them; he was small, crawling in front of the houses, and a stone struck him and killed him.
The Prophet ﷺ said: (And the first blood I set aside (1) is the blood of the son of Rabīʿah ibn al-Ḥārith (2)) .
It is narrated that he said of him: (Ādam) . He saw in ⟦1:257⟧ the book the blood of the son of Rabīʿah and added an alif, and the apparent explanation is that, because of his youth, his name was not remembered.
It was also said: His name was Tammām ibn Rabīʿah (1) .
They said: Rabīʿah was two years older than his uncle al-ʿAbbās, and at the time of Badr Rabīʿah was absent in Syria.
Ibn Saʿd said: When al-ʿAbbās and Nawfal set out to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ as emigrants in the days of the Trench, Rabīʿah saw them off as far as al-Abwāʾ, then wanted to return.
They said to him: Where will you return? To the abode of polytheism, fighting the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and denying him, when he has become mighty and his companions numerous? Turn back.
So he travelled with them until they all arrived as Muslims.
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ granted Rabīʿah at Khaybar one hundred wasqs every year, and he was present with him at the conquest and at Ḥunayn, and built a house in Medina.
He died in the caliphate (الخلافة) of ʿUmar (2) .
It is narrated that the Prophet ﷺ said: (What an excellent servant Rabīʿah ibn al-Ḥārith is, if only he would shorten his hair and hitch up his garment (3)) .
Rabīʿah was a partner of ʿUthmān in trade, and it has come in the hadith of Jābir that is in ⟦1:258⟧ the rites of pilgrimage: (And the first blood I set aside is the blood (1) of the son of Rabīʿah ibn al-Ḥārith) .
He meant the one for whom Rabīʿah was entitled to blood-money (الدية) on account of his son.
It was also said: He died in the year 13.
His mother was Ghuzayyah bint Qays ibn Ṭarīf.

51.h: 47 - ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Ḥārith ibn ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib al-Hāshimī *
51.t:
The brother of Rabīʿah and Nawfal.
His name was ʿAbd Shams, and it was changed; they narrated that he emigrated shortly before the conquest, and the Prophet ﷺ named him ʿAbd Allāh.
He went out with the Prophet ﷺ on some of his campaigns, and died at al-Ṣafrāʾ, and he shrouded him in his shirt - meaning: the shirt of the Prophet ﷺ.
It has been said that he said of him: (He is fortunate; fortune has reached him (2)) .
Ibn Saʿd reported this thus, without a chain of transmission (إسناد).
And this man has no offspring.

52.h: 48 - Khālid ibn Saʿīd ibn al-ʿĀṣ ibn Umayyah al-Umawī **
52.t:
Ibn ʿAbd Shams ibn ʿAbd Manāf ibn Quṣayy, ⟦1:259⟧ the great chief, Abū Saʿīd al-Qurashī, al-Umawī, one of the first forerunners.
It is narrated from Umm Khālid bint Khālid, who said:
My father was the fifth in Islam, and he emigrated to the land of Abyssinia and stayed there for more than ten years, and I was born there (1) .
Ibrāhīm ibn ʿUqbah narrated, from Umm Khālid, who said:
My father was the first to write: In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.
It is narrated that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ appointed him over Ṣanʿāʾ, and that Abū Bakr made him commander over part of the army in the raid on Syria.
Mūsā ibn ʿUqbah said: Our elders informed us:
That Khālid killed a polytheist, then wore his spoils of brocade or silk, and the people looked at him as he was with ʿAmr.
He said: What is it with you that you look? Whoever wishes, let him do the like of Khālid’s deed, then wear his clothing.
It is narrated that when Khālid (may Allah be pleased with him) was martyred, the man who killed him, after he had become a Muslim, said:
Who was this man? For I saw a light of his shining up to the sky.
It was also said: Khālid ibn Saʿīd was handsome and good-looking; he was killed on the day of Ajnādayn, and he emigrated with Jaʿfar ibn Abī Ṭālib to Medina at the time of Khaybar, and his daughter mentioned lived long and survived until near the year 90.
His father Abū Uḥayḥah was one of the great men of the Jāhiliyyah (الجاهلية); he died before the expedition of Badr as a polytheist.
He had several children, among them: ⟦1:260⟧

53.t:
Abū al-Walīd al-Umawī, whose acceptance of Islam was delayed; he was a wealthy merchant who travelled to Syria, and he was the one who gave protection to his cousin ʿUthmān ibn ʿAffān on the day of al-Ḥudaybiyah when the Prophet ﷺ sent him as an envoy to Mecca; Abān met him, saying:
Come forward and proceed, and fear no one ... the Banū Saʿīd are the mighty ones of the land (1)
Then he became a Muslim on the day of the conquest, or rather before the conquest, and emigrated, and that was because his two brothers, Khālid mentioned above and ʿAmr, when they came from the emigration to Abyssinia to Medina, sent to him calling him to Allah the Exalted, so he hastened and came to Medina as a Muslim.
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ appointed him in the year 9 over Bahrain.
Then he was martyred, he and his brother Khālid, on the day of Ajnādayn, according to the authentic (الصحيح) view.
Abān was the son of the paternal aunt of Abū Jahl.
And their brother:

54.h: 50 - ʿAmr ibn Saʿīd ibn al-ʿĀṣ al-Umawī **
54.t:
He had two emigrations: to Abyssinia, then to Medina, and he has a hadith in the Musnad of the Imam Aḥmad (Musnad al-Imām ⟦1:261⟧ Aḥmad).
He was martyred on the day of al-Yarmūk - and it is said: on the day of Ajnādayn - with his two brothers (may Allah be pleased with them).
ʿAmr ibn Saʿīd al-Ashdaq narrated:
That his paternal uncles Khālid, Abān and ʿAmr returned from their posts when the death of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ reached them.
Abū Bakr said: No one is more entitled to the work than the officials of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ; return to your posts.
They refused and left for Syria, and were killed (may Allah be pleased with them).
